narrative.overview:
Church Presenter is the room behind the room. The sanctuary is dim, the service is happening, and the operator's screen must glow just enough to work by without spilling light or attention. Everything sits on a neutral graphite near-black, with solid graphite cards and a floating sidebar above it. Light is spent only where hands and eyes are needed: the near-white primary on the one action that matters, Live Green on the slide the congregation is seeing, and nothing else competing.

The system is dense, like a mixing console, but never cramped. Labels are small and uppercase, controls are compact, and the canvas or current-output frame is always the largest, brightest thing on screen. Inter carries the whole app, interface and audience output alike: bold for titles, semibold for headings and controls, tabular figures for numbers. Slide content keeps its own serif option (Noto Serif), separate from the interface.

Controls are quiet until needed. Ghost and outlined buttons recede into the surface. Only the primary white action and the live state carry visual weight, so a volunteer can find "what do I press next" at a glance.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite base (Sanctuary Dark) with solid graphite cards; glass only on chrome.
One action voice: the near-white primary (code name `--amber`) for action, selected navigation, and focus.
Three reserved state colors: green means live, violet means selected, red means destructive.
One family, Inter, with bold headings and tabular figures for dense data.
Dense, console-like spacing on a 4px rhythm. The 16:9 canvas is always the focal point.

rules.name: The One Source Rule
rules.body: Never hand-type an `rgba()` of an existing family. Use `rgb(var(--family-rgb) / alpha)`. Only shadow black, highlight white, button gradient stops and slide background art stay literal.

rules.name: The Green Means Live Rule
rules.body: Use Live Green for audience-visible state, paired with a visible live label or dot.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The near-white primary action provides emphasis; reserve green for live output, violet for selection and red for destructive actions.

rules.name: The No Pure White Rule
rules.body: Use the text color tokens for operator content and keep contrast legible against dark surfaces.

rules.name: The 11px Floor Rule
rules.body: No operator-facing text is smaller than 11px. The booth is dim, and the screen is often a laptop across a desk. Slide content on the canvas is exempt because it scales with the canvas.

rules.name: The Steady Digits Rule
rules.body: Clocks, timers, slide positions, and counts use tabular numerals so they don't shift while live.

rules.name: The Canvas Is the Center Rule
rules.body: In the editor and in live mode, the 16:9 slide is the largest element on screen at every width. Panels give up space before the canvas does.

rules.name: The Reflow, Never Hide Rule
rules.body: Narrow widths move panels; they never remove a feature. The inspector, rundown, next slide, and history must be reachable at every size.

rules.name: The Ambient Only Rule
rules.body: Use soft shadows and restrained highlights to distinguish layered controls and live output.

rules.name: The Seven Corners Rule
rules.body: Use a `--rounded-*` step, never a raw pixel radius. Slide content on the canvas is exempt because it scales with the canvas.

dos: **Do** keep Live Green exclusively for audience-visible state, always with a "LIVE" word or dot.
**Do** use Selection Violet for selected or editing state: rundown row, canvas element, active tab.
**Do** limit each view to one filled primary button. Make everything else secondary, ghost, or a link.
**Do** set screen titles, service names, dialog titles, and panel titles and interactive controls in Inter.
**Do** keep operator text at 11px or larger, and use tabular numerals for anything that counts or ticks.
**Do** use neutral hairlines (8–15% opacity) for borders and the 9px / 14px radius pair for controls and panels.
**Do** reflow panels at narrow widths. The canvas stays the largest thing on screen.
**Do** respect the Reduce Transparency and Reduce Motion settings. Both must keep working.
donts: **Don't** use green for success toasts, "saved" states, or selection.
**Don't** leave native grey form controls. Every select and input takes the recessed dark field style.
**Don't** add hard offset shadows or colored glows beyond the primary action lift and the live frame glow.
**Don't** hide the inspector, rundown, next slide, or history at small widths. Move them instead.
**Don't** set operator UI text below 11px, and don't put a second framed focus box inside an already-framed field.
